title: Pull out both handles of an over-the-sink colander and bridge it across a sink basin
instruction: Pull out the extendable handles of the colander and rest both handles across the left and right rims of the sink so the colander hangs suspended over the basin.
context: Home cooks and commercial food-prep workers expand telescoping over-the-sink colanders across open sink basins so produce can be rinsed or pasta drained hands-free above the sink floor without tipping.
setup: Two 1:1 kitchen objects on the station bench (external colander dimensions, 0.77 kg mass, crimped stainless friction-slide sleeves, and four downward handle rubber feet plus four base rubber feet follow Norpro #2158 Expanding Colander with Base Frame; zero adapted pickup bosses): (1) Fixed stainless countertop sink-basin module (585 mm wide along Y x 300 mm along X x 125 mm tall at x=435 mm, y=0 mm, rim height TOP + 125 mm) with a 455 x 276 mm open rectangular basin (y=-227.5..+227.5 mm, floor at TOP + 6 mm) flanked by 65 mm-wide flat left and right sink deck ledges (y=+227.5..+292.5 mm and y=-292.5..-227.5 mm); (2) Loose 0.77 kg stainless over-the-sink colander (236 x 230 x 120 mm slatted perforated basket on four rubber base feet plus two 105 mm-stroke sliding stainless U-rod handles in crimped friction-slide sleeves with four downward corner rubber rest feet, starting collapsed at 340 mm overall span on the front counter at x=155 mm, y=0 mm, 15 mm clear in front of the sink apron). Collapsed (340 mm) or extended on one side only (445 mm), the colander is narrower than the 455 mm basin opening and drops onto the basin floor.
scoring: Latched 0 only if any collider of the colander strikes the station tabletop, floor, or sink basin floor with a pre-impact downward speed exceeding 0.50 m/s or falls off the bench; recoverable rim contact or gentle counter placement never penalizes the trial, and any hand assignment or symmetric/asymmetric two-arm extension split is valid. Every positive score requires both gripper pad midpoints and all four independent jaw endpoints >=80 mm from every collider surface of the colander and sink module, and <1 mm 3D Euclidean corner-point movement across the basket and both sliding handles over the final 1.0 s (21 samples at 20 Hz). 0.40: combined handle extension (arm_left + arm_right) >=135 mm (overall span >=475 mm, exceeding the 455 mm basin opening). 1.0: both extended handle rubber-foot bars seated flat on the left (y>=+227.5 mm) and right (y<=-227.5 mm) sink deck rims (>=17.5 mm bearing overlap past each inner rim wall, colander tilt <=5.0 degrees, basket centered within 40 mm of x=435 mm, and basket bottom suspended >=15 mm clear above the sink basin floor).
reset_notes: Lift the colander off the sink rims, push both sliding handles fully inward to the 340 mm collapsed span, and place it centred on its rubber base feet at x=155 mm, y=0 mm.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX primitives match Norpro #2158 expanding over-the-sink colander envelope and mass (340x230x120 mm collapsed, expanding to 550 mm, 0.77 kg) with crimped stainless friction-slide sleeves and downward rubber handle/base feet (zero adapted pickup bosses). Sink module dimensions (585x300x125 mm, 455x276 mm basin), sub-masses, and slide-collar friction (1.6 N) are engineering estimates; water/produce rinsing is omitted.
